queries.query: how does each little organism decide which way to turn — does it look straight ahead and off to each side before it moves?
queries.why: stepAgents samples the field at a forward point and two flanking points offset by the sensor angle, then turns toward whichever reads strongest.

queries.query: when one instrument drops out of the mix, what makes its part of the picture fade down without disappearing entirely?
queries.why: The multiplier is floor + (1 - floor) * activity^curve with a default floor of 0.25 — explicitly 'a floor, not a gate', so a silent instrument keeps a ghost rather than blacking out.

queries.query: a user's edits were never being written to storage because changes kept streaming in and reset the timer forever — what bounds the wait so a write eventually lands?
queries.why: The header documents the trailing-debounce starvation failure ('my exposure settings are lost on reload') and maxWaitMs (default 2000) sets a deadline timer once dirty so the write happens regardless of the change stream.

queries.query: why would the same song come out with mirrored axes on two different runs, and what pins the orientation down?
queries.why: The decomposition notes that SVD leaves each direction's sign arbitrary so an unconstrained run flips axes between runs and tracks; the fix forces the largest-magnitude loading in each direction positive.

queries.query: the human just points at whichever variation looks better and the system keeps moving that way — how does that steering work when there is no objective function to optimize?
queries.why: Documented as a (1+lambda) evolution strategy with lambda = 8 over a black box with a noisy ordinal oracle: sample around the incumbent, keep the winner, and repeat the winning displacement as a free line search.

queries.query: pulling rendered images back off the graphics card leaves each line of pixels padded out to an alignment boundary — where is that padding removed so consumers get tightly packed bytes?
queries.why: COPY_BYTES_PER_ROW_ALIGNMENT = 256 drives the padded/unpadded row layout, and stripReadbackRowPadding copies row by row from the staging buffer into a tightly packed output.

queries.query: the picture was landing slightly before you could hear the hit — how is the gap between handing samples to the sound hardware and actually hearing them accounted for?
queries.why: outputDelay() adds baseLatency plus outputLatency into the time origin, with the comment that without it the simulation leads the audio by 20-50 ms on WASAPI and drops land early.

queries.query: what keeps two mutually attracting groups from crushing themselves into a single point within a few frames?
queries.why: REPULSE = 3.0 is a universal sign-blind short-range term applied to every pair — the comment states that without it two mutually attracted kinds collapse to a point — and the force law makes it divergent toward contact rather than linearly capped.

queries.query: if you jump forward a couple of seconds in the track, why doesn't everything that would have happened in the skipped stretch all fire at once?
queries.why: A gap larger than MAX_WALK_GAP_TICKS is treated as a seek and relocates the pointer by binary search, discarding what was skipped — the comment names the exact failure of walking instead (two seconds of hats and kicks firing together).

queries.query: a song fetched once still plays later even with the machine that served it switched off — where does that storage layer live?
queries.why: The module stores whole HTTP responses (a ~200 KB manifest, ~600 KB binary and ~40 MB of audio) in the Cache API with only a small index in localStorage, and cachingFetch is the read-through the loader and the transport call instead of fetch.

queries.query: glow around the brightest filaments used to snap on and off as they crossed the cutoff — how was that made a gradual transition?
queries.why: fsPrefilter uses a soft-knee threshold (credited to Karis) whose quadratic transition replaces a hard threshold that made the effect pop on and off as a filament crossed it, which read as flicker.

queries.query: how is a per-stem activity curve built from RMS loudness and onset strength?
queries.why: activity_from_curves combines a dB-domain level with a gated onset boost and then an asymmetric EMA with fast attack and slow release.

queries.query: what does the slew limiter do to modulated parameters, and what are the fast / medium / slow time constants?
queries.why: SlewLimiter applies exponential approach per parameter class with DEFAULT_SLEW = { fast: 0.05, medium: 0.5, slow: 8 }, plus snapClass for section boundaries.

queries.query: how is the seed resolved at startup — does a URL query parameter beat a pinned seed?
queries.why: resolveSeed checks ?seed= first, then the localStorage pin, then a fresh random seed; syncUrlSeed only rewrites the parameter when it is already present.

queries.query: which PQ / ST 2084 transfer function constants does the HDR10 export path use?
queries.why: PQ_M1/PQ_M2/PQ_C1/PQ_C2/PQ_C3 are declared in exact rational form with pqEncodeNits and pqDecodeNits implementing the inverse EOTF and EOTF against a 10,000-nit peak.

queries.query: how does the driver bank z-score its channels and reorder the latent components by variance?
queries.why: The module header describes the ~16-channel named bank (novelty4, novelty16, chorus-ness plus the top ~13 components), z-scoring per track, and re-measuring variance at load because post-PCA smoothing broke the stored ordering.

queries.query: how does the analysis server compute the track content version the browser caches on?
queries.why: timeline_content_version sha256s timeline.json and timeline.bin and truncates to 16 hex chars; track_entry memoises it on (size, mtime_ns) and explains why it is a content hash rather than an mtime.

queries.query: where is smoothDtFrames defined?
queries.why: Exported function that smooths the render frame length in 60 Hz units, with the DT_FRAMES_TAU_S constant above it.

queries.query: which shader file contains the stepAgents compute entry point?
queries.why: @compute @workgroup_size(64) fn stepAgents is declared there, alongside initAgents, respawnAgents and splashAgents.

queries.query: where is the followMultiplier function implemented?
queries.why: Exported pure helper returning floor + (1 - floor) * pow(activity, curve), used by the StemFollow class in the same file.

queries.query: where does maxChromaForLh live?
queries.why: Module-private function in the vendored HSLuv transcription, taking the inner envelope of the six gamut boundary lines; called by hsluvToRgb and rgbToHsluv.

queries.query: which layer of the music model did the research settle on, and why not the final layer?
queries.why: Both cite arXiv 2505.16306's per-layer probing table: layer ~6 for genre/emotion character, layers 9-12 for structural identity, and the finding that the best layer is almost never the last.

queries.query: why did we stop projecting straight from the raw 1024-dimensional embedding and introduce a bank of named signals instead?
queries.why: plan.md Revision 4 records the reason ('raw-1024 random projections react to everything and isolate nothing; nobody can tune 1024 weights') and the implementation header repeats it as the rationale for the named, gain-per-channel tuning surface.

queries.query: did the HDR video export end up shipping on HEVC or AV1, and what was wrong with the earlier conclusion?
queries.why: The 2026-08-13 correction states the earlier HEVC conclusion was caused by an old local FFmpeg, that av1_metadata has existed since FFmpeg 4.3, and that the shipped profiles are now av1-hdr10-2160p120 / av1-hdr10-1080p120 with hevc_nvenc removed entirely.

queries.query: why was HSLuv chosen over OKLCh for the species palette?
queries.why: The handoff records the decision (every H,S,L triple is inside sRGB by construction and equal-L hues have equal perceived lightness, matching the vuzic prior art), and oklch.ts states the same trade-off from the other side.
